label: Feline (domestic cat)

image.author: MichalPL
image.species_shown: Felis catus, adult domestic cat (black-and-white, outdoors on grass)
image.view: Standing three-quarter view from the side, all four legs and the tail visible, head turned toward the camera. Viewed at https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Domestic_cat_in_Poland_1.jpg/1280px-Domestic_cat_in_Poland_1.jpg
image.image_observations: The photo shows an adult black-and-white cat standing on grass, seen from the side and slightly from the front, with the head turned toward the camera. Belly height is roughly half the withers height, so the torso is lower and shallower than a simple ellipsoid centred high on the legs would give. The rump top sits a little below the withers, the hocks are raised with only the toes on the ground, and the tail hangs behind to about the level of the paws. These cues set the hip, stifle, elbow and tail-base heights in this revision; the low camera angle and head turn mean the photo gives proportions only, not exact lengths.

physical_parsing.volume_method: Torso as a solid ellipsoid with semi-axes 0.23 m (length), 0.06 m (depth, back to belly), 0.055 m (width): 4/3 * pi * a * b * c = 0.0032 m3, plus limbs, head and tail, giving about 0.0045 m3. This matches a 4-5 kg adult at water density. Dimensions are from the size source, with the vertical placement of the torso taken from the photo.
physical_parsing.shape_class: Quadruped, digitigrade, elongate torso on four slender legs, with a long tail and a rounded head. Plantigrade hindfoot is not assumed: the hock is raised and only the toes contact the ground.

core.description: Elongate torso ellipsoid spanning the thorax (forelimb girdle) to the pelvis (hindlimb girdle). In the photo the belly sits about 0.11 m above the ground and the withers about 0.23 m, so the core is centred near 0.17 m height, not at the ground. Head is a separate rounded mass on a short neck, attached at the anterior end of the core. Tail base is a posterior extension of the sacrum, at rump height.
core.cross_section: Elliptical, about 0.11 m wide by 0.12 m deep at the thorax (belly about 0.11 m to back about 0.23 m above the ground), narrowing slightly at the lumbar region

physical_parsing.size_source: Wikipedia 'Cat' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat): adult head-body length about 46 cm, height at shoulder 23-25 cm, tail about 30 cm, weight 4-5 kg. Cross-checked with Felidae Fund (https://felidaefund.org/learn/cats/domestic-cat): length 46-51 cm, shoulder height 20-25 cm. Values are approximate; adult sizes vary by breed and sex. Bounding box uses the head-body length plus tail, so length_z is 0.46 + 0.30 = 0.76 m. Vertical placement of the torso, hips and tail base is from the photo, not the size source.

parts.name: Forelimb (left)

penetration.overlap_region: Lateral thoracic wall and scapular region of the core, roughly 0.02 m inboard of the core's +X surface at z 0.27-0.33

parts.notes: Digitigrade: the carpus is raised about 0.06 m off the ground and only the digits contact the floor, so the lower leg behaves like a short lever. Shoulder has no bony clavicle; the scapula floats on muscle and is attached by a ball-like muscular joint. Joint ranges are approximate, from published cat gait kinematics and general mammal anatomy, not measured. In the photo the elbow sits at about belly height, so the elbow joint was lowered to 0.50 of box height (about 0.135 m).

parts.name: Hindlimb (left)

penetration.overlap_region: Pelvic girdle and lateral flank of the core, roughly 0.025 m inboard of the core's +X surface at z -0.08 to 0.02

parts.notes: Digitigrade hindleg with the hock raised about 0.08 m off the ground. The hock is the high joint behind the knee, and the foot contacts ground only through the toes. The hip is a deep ball joint inside the pelvis, so the thigh is the thickest part of the leg. The stifle is largely hidden in the flank, and its range is approximate. The photo puts the rump top a little below the withers (hip near 0.21 m), so the hip was lowered from 0.90 to 0.78 of box height, and the stifle to 0.43 (about 0.12 m), near belly level.

parts.name: Paw pads (left)

penetration.overlap_region: Distal metapodials at the sole of the foot, not the core. Pads are a surface feature with a shallow seat.

parts.notes: Count is 2 per side: one fore paw and one hind paw pad group. Each pad group has a central metacarpal/metatarsal pad and digital pads, and the cushions take impact and give grip. They are modelled as one surface per paw. Count 2 per side is an assumption based on the two paws on each side of the body.

parts.name: Retractable claws (left)

penetration.overlap_region: Distal phalanx tip of each digit, not the core

parts.notes: Forefoot has 5 digits and the hindfoot has 4 (the dewclaw is on the forelimb). Claws retract by a ligament mechanism, so the claw is folded inside a sheath unless extended. The count shown is forefoot only; the hindfoot has 4 claws. Claw length is about 1 cm. Used for grasping prey and climbing.

parts.name: Tail

penetration.overlap_region: Posterior-dorsal sacral end of the core, z -0.12 to -0.14

parts.notes: Balance tail used for steering while running and climbing. Mobile base, with most of the length free. Range is approximate. No library tail fits a slim, flexible tail; tail_tuft is fluffy and tail_club is blunt, so both were rejected. Tail base was lowered to 0.67 of box height (about 0.18 m) to match the rump top in the photo. In the photo the tail is about 0.6 of body length, close to the 0.30 m source value.

parts.name: Eye (left)

penetration.overlap_region: Orbit in the head mass, set into the forward-facing face of the head

parts.notes: Forward-facing with binocular overlap for depth. Pupil is a vertical slit in bright light and round in dim light. Eye is very large relative to the head. Visible on the front of the head.

parts.name: Ear (left)

penetration.overlap_region: Top corner of the head mass, cartilaginous base

parts.notes: Upright, mobile, triangular pinnae that can rotate independently for directional hearing. Closest library fit is ear_leaf, although the cat ear is a rigid cartilage cone rather than a leaf. The pinna base is mobile at the ball joint.

parts.name: Whiskers (vibrissae, left)

penetration.overlap_region: Follicle seated in the muzzle pad at the front of the head

parts.notes: Several rows of long, stiff vibrissae on each side of the muzzle, each seated in a follicle with a dense nerve supply. They sense touch and air movement. No library part for thin radiating whiskers. Count is per side, with several whiskers per row.

parts.name: Nose (rhinarium)

penetration.overlap_region: Nasal bone and anterior tip of the skull, at the front of the head

parts.notes: Moist, pigmented rhinarium at the front of the muzzle. It is part of the olfactory system, not a separate mechanical feature. Cat nose is a small pad, not a snout.

parts.name: Jaws and canines

penetration.overlap_region: Mandibular condyle and jaw musculature in the head mass

parts.notes: Short skull with a strong hinge jaw. Long upper and lower canines for piercing and holding prey, and carnassial teeth for shearing meat, used in a vertical bite. Gape is limited, and the hinge is a simple up-down joint. Canines are the main prey-killing structure.

parts.name: Fur coat and patterning

penetration.overlap_region: Surface skin layer over the whole body, not a separate mesh
penetration.notes: Set to 0: a surface covering does not penetrate the core.

parts.notes: Patterning and coat length are surface detail, not a structure. Listed here only so the aesthetics category is documented. Not a mesh part and not counted in the summary. Penetration depth is 0 because a surface covering does not seat into the core.

constraints.symmetry: Bilateral about the sagittal plane (X=0). Limbs, eyes, ears and whiskers are mirrored. Tail, nose and jaws are on the midline.
constraints.gait: Walk and trot as diagonal-couplet pacing; gallop is rotary with a flexible spine. Digitigrade legs with the hock and carpus raised off the ground, so only the toes contact the floor.
other: Hindfoot has 4 claws and forefoot 5; claw count is recorded once per limb side.
Joint ranges are approximate and come from general mammalian kinematics; they are not measured from a cat gait study.
Size and proportions are for a typical adult domestic cat and do not match large felids such as tiger or leopard.

library_gaps.why: No library tail fits. tail_tuft is fluffy and tail_club is blunt.
No library part for thin, radiating, stiff whiskers.

library_gaps.feature: Head (rounded skull with forward eyes, mounted on a short neck)
library_gaps.why: No library head/cranium part. Only eyes, ears and jaws are represented.
